body:
Please use the bash command in the readme of `eslint-config-airbnb` to install all the proper peer deps - reproduced here (i'm pretty sure i mentioned it in another issue as well):

``` sh
(
  export PKG=eslint-config-airbnb;
  npm info "$PKG" peerDependencies --json | command sed 's/[\{\},]//g ; s/: /@/g' | xargs npm install --save-dev "$PKG"
)
```

I highly recommend reusing that command for anything you install that might have peer deps.
@ljharb We can't use this command, since it wouldn't work on Windows. I'm not even sure it would work on OSX without some additional installations.
@ilyavolodin it absolutely works on stock OS X as well as any POSIX system with npm installed. You're right about Windows, but you can reimplement that command in JS pretty trivially, as shown above.
Ok, I have no objections to doing it the way @vitorbal showed. To answer your question, yes, we should assume that npm executable is present.

@miqmago yes, that's the current cause. however, because eslint configs need to use peerDeps, any time a breaking change peerDep of the config is released, this problem will re-present itself, unless `--init` explicitly installs the peer deps that the intended config version depends on.
